eval-bot: Nightly eval job (2026-03-19T04:00Z) detected a regression cluster: model-rw-3@v12.1 + int8 quant config shows ~18% of prompt-set failures vs v12.0-fp16 baseline. Failing suites: instr-follow-small, code-snippets-100, convo-reply-short. Attaching minimal examples.
anika: Ugh. Quick check — are these failures primarily truncation/shift in the first 6 tokens or semantic divergence later in generations?
maya: Reproduced locally. Behavior looks like an off-by-one token alignment at generation start for many prompts. Example diff (token ids):
```
# baseline (v12.0 fp16)
>> tokenizer.encode(" def greet():")
[345, 18, 902, 6, ...]

# v12.1 + int8 quant
>> tokenizer.encode(" def greet():")
[11, 345, 18, 902, 6, ...]
```
So an extra small-id token is being prepended by the tokenizer path in v12.1 for certain whitespace-prefixed inputs.
sam: Is this the tokenizer or the quantized inference runner shuffling the KV/offsets? Two hypotheses: 1) tokenizer vocab reorder (rare) 2) quantized embedding table index mapping got misaligned in the converter.
leo: I ran a quick compare on raw embedding lookups (fp16 weights loaded into same runtime but using v12.1 tokenizer) — that reproduces the prepended-id behavior. So points to tokenizer/tokenizer-normalizer change rather than weight quantization mapping.
anika: Good detective work. Can you paste the tokenizer config diff? maybe a new normalizer or leading-space-preserve flag was toggled.
leo: Config snippet:
```
- normalizer: "strip_leading_space: true"
+ normalizer: "strip_leading_space: false"
```
That flip would change how leading spaces are handled; the extra token looks like our special space marker (id=11).
maya: That explains it. Many of our instruction prompts start with a leading space (we use it to bias formatting). If the normalizer stopped stripping the space, tokenizer turns it into explicit token 11 and shifts subsequent ids.
sam: Impact matrix: affects any prompt with leading-space-prepended instructions AND any evaluation that expects answer in specific token offsets (short completions). Degrades BLEU/Perplexity on those suites.
infra-bot: nightly-deployer: pinned model-rw-3@v12.0-fp16 for production traffic at 2026-03-19T04:10Z due to quality regression alert.
anika: Immediate mitigation options:
- revert tokenizer config in v12.1 and regenerate tokenizer artifacts (fast)
- add a compatibility shim in runtime to strip leading space tokens when matching older routing (less ideal)
- update eval prompt sets to normalize-leading-space (but this changes the benchmark, not fix model behavior)

maya: I can push a quick patch that enforces legacy strip behavior during serving: small wrapper in tokenizer_loader that sets normalizer.strip_leading_space=true when model metadata.compat_mode == "v12-legacy". Will run unit tests.
sam: Please also run a small quant-check: run int8 conversion with the regenerated tokenizer to ensure no indexing mismatch in embedding table mapping.
leo: I'll start a rollout plan: test patch on staging with the full eval harness (all failing suites) and if green, opt for a targeted rebuild of v12.1 tokenizer artifacts and flip the model package.
anika: Can someone open an internal issue and tag infra + runtime? Assign to maya for hotfix and leo for rollout coordination. Also add a note to model-onboarding checklist to include 'leading space normalization parity' tests.
maya: Issue created: ML-4567 "v12.1 tokenizer leading-space parity causing eval regressions". PR coming in ~30m. Patch will be in the hotfix branch.
leo: I'll queue staging run now. ETA ~45m for full eval pass.
anika: Thanks team. If staging passes, we'll coordinate a canary redeploy to 5% traffic and watch Console metrics (token-level loss and short-completion mismatch) for 1 hour before wider rollout. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: started staging run for model-rw-3@v12.1-hotfix at 2026-03-19T04:25Z.
